```{r preprocessing}
# function to parse html and clean text

  parse_fn <- function(.html){
    read_html(.html) %>%
      html_elements('p') %>%
      html_text2() %>%
      str_c(collapse = ' ') %>%
      rm_url() %>%
      rm_email() %>%
      str_remove_all('\'') %>%
      str_replace_all(paste(c('\n', 
                              '[[:punct:]]', 
                              'nbsp', 
                              '[[:digit:]]', 
                              '[[:symbol:]]'),
                            collapse = '|'), ' ') %>%
      str_replace_all("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2") %>%
      tolower() %>%
      str_replace_all("\\s+", " ")
  }

  
  # function to apply to claims data
  parse_data <- function(.df){
    out <- .df %>%
      filter(str_detect(text_tmp, '<!')) %>%
      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(text_clean = parse_fn(text_tmp)) %>%
      unnest(text_clean) 
    return(out)
  }

nlp_fn <- function(parse_data.out){
  out <- parse_data.out %>% 
    unnest_tokens(output = token, 
                  input = text_clean, 
                  token = 'words',
                  stopwords = str_remove_all(stop_words$word, 
                                             '[[:punct:]]')) %>%
    mutate(token.lem = lemmatize_words(token)) %>%
    filter(str_length(token.lem) > 2) %>%
    count(.id, bclass, token.lem, name = 'n') %>%
    bind_tf_idf(term = token.lem, 
                document = .id,
                n = n) %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c('.id', 'bclass'),
                names_from = 'token.lem',
                values_from = 'tf_idf',
                values_fill = 0)
  return(out)
}
```

```{r }
#Augment the HTML scraping strategy so that header information is captured in addition to paragraph content. Are binary class predictions improved using logistic principal component regression?

# second fn to include headers
 parse_fn2 <- function(.html){
    read_html(.html) %>%
      html_elements('h1, p') %>%
      html_text2() %>%
      str_c(collapse = ' ') %>%
      rm_url() %>%
      rm_email() %>%
      str_remove_all('\'') %>%
      str_replace_all(paste(c('\n', 
                              '[[:punct:]]', 
                              'nbsp', 
                              '[[:digit:]]', 
                              '[[:symbol:]]'),
                            collapse = '|'), ' ') %>%
      str_replace_all("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2") %>%
      tolower() %>%
      str_replace_all("\\s+", " ")
 }

# claims with the header included
claims_raw %>%
  head(1) %>%
  filter(str_detect(text_tmp, '<!')) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(text_clean = parse_fn2(text_tmp)) %>%
  unnest(text_clean) |>
  select(text_tmp, text_clean) |>
  pull(text_clean) 

  parse_data2 <- function(.df, chunk_size = 250){
    safe_parse <- possibly(parse_fn2, otherwise = NA_character_)

  .df <- .df %>% filter(str_detect(text_tmp, '<!'))

  # create a list of row-number vectors to index data
  # seq_len(nrow(.df)) gives the vector of row numbers
  # chunk_size is 250
  # ceiling(seq_len(nrow(.df)) / chunk_size) splits the sequence of rows into chunks of 250 and ceiling rounds up to next whole number
  # split(x,f) divides the vector x into a list, one element per distinct label in f
  # so idx is a list of integer vectors which correspond to the row numbers of the data
  idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(.df)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(.df)) / chunk_size))

  text_clean <- vector("list", length(idx)) # this creates an empty list with one slot per chunk
  
  for (i in seq_along(idx)) { # iterate along the chunks 
    # for every i chunk, map the safe_parse function to the rows pulled by the corresponding chunk
    text_clean[[i]] <- map_chr(.df$text_tmp[idx[[i]]], safe_parse) 
    gc() # refresh memory
  }
  
  # create text_clean column by unlisting the text_clean list and storing
  .df$text_clean <- unlist(text_clean)
  .df
}
```

```{r log regression}
## LOGISTIC REGRESSION
#######################

# select subset of interest
# partition into training and test set


# pull the stop words from tidy text
stpwrd <- stop_words |>
  pull(word) |> 
  str_remove_all('[[:punct:]]')

claims_dtm <- claims_clean2 |>
  select(.id, bclass, mclass, text_clean) |>
  unnest_tokens(output = token, input = text_clean, token = 'words', stopwords = stpwrd) |>
  mutate(token = lemmatize_words(token)) |>
  count(.id, token) |>
  bind_tf_idf(term = token, document = .id, n = n) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = .id, names_from = token, values_from = tf_idf, values_fill = 0) 

claims_new <- claims_clean2 |>
  select(.id, bclass, mclass) |>
  inner_join(claims_dtm, by = ".id")

set.seed(101422)
claims_split <- claims_new %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)


test_dtm <- testing(claims_split) %>%
  select(-.id, -bclass, -mclass)
test_labels <- testing(claims_split) %>%
  select(.id, bclass, mclass)

# same, training set
train_dtm <- training(claims_split) %>%
  select(-.id, -bclass, -mclass)
train_labels <- training(claims_split) %>%
  select(.id, bclass, mclass)

train_dtm |> head(5)
train_dtm_test <- train_dtm[1:1000]

# find projections based on training data
proj_out <- projection_fn(.dtm = train_dtm, .prop = 0.7) # this code will capture 70%
train_dtm_projected <- proj_out$data

# how many components were used?
proj_out$n_pc

# fit logistic regression model to training set
fit <- glm(bclass ~ ., 
           data = training(claims_split), 
           family = 'binomial')

# evaluate errors on test set
class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)

testing(biomarker_split) %>%
  add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') %>% 
  mutate(estimate = factor(pred >0.5, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
         truth = factor(class, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))) %>%
  class_metrics(estimate = estimate,
                truth = truth, pred,
                event_level = 'second')
```
